prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant: continuous compliant supply/visibility/safe automation/manual intervention; boundary River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood)/Raw Water Screen Channel–High Service Pump Header; distribution excluded. Intake requires demand/withdrawal/depth/equipment/downstream limits, healthy motor/open paths/interlocks; low-level/fault/local-control inhibit; lost permissives alarm/stop. Screen monitors level/differential/rake/debris; sends Rake Torque Snapshot; high-high requires field confirmation. Chief Operator authorizes Storm Intake Mode/urgent large-dose corrections; confirms recovery before normal service. Coagulant Dosing Skid (Marigold) sends Alum Batch Ticket; Laboratory Technician verifies lot identity. Small dose increments; verified-feedback trimming; feedback loss uses last-safe/approved-fixed dose plus grabs. Duty Engineer approves temporary rapid-turbidity adjustments/configuration/forecasts; reviews consequential field/laboratory discrepancies. North Filter Gallery (Cobalt) records turbidity/headloss; South Filter Gallery sends Filter Run Exception Note; both receive advisories; backwash considers duration/headloss/turbidity/upstream; return requires compliant rinse/stability. Overrides require justification/monitoring/prompt restoration. Chlorine Contact Basin: assess coagulation/disinfection impacts; Chlorine Residual Alarm requires immediate assessment/prioritized independent grabs. Clearwell Level Controller coordinates storage/production; Distribution Dispatcher receives restrictions before header impacts. Maintenance Planner schedules poststorm work. Chemical Supplier Driver delivers chemicals; Residuals Hauler removes material. Backwash Recovery Tank recovers backwash; sample after consequential return-to-process events. Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (Sparrow) receives custody-controlled samples from six treatment locations; verifies schedule/labels/container/holding-time/temperature/preservation/seal; sends date/time/identifier-checked Jar Test Photograph Set. Laboratory Technician sends complete/legible Sample Chain Slip; records label/log/operator-note mismatches before acceptance; preserves custody/acceptance records for Chief Operator/Duty Engineer/regulatory auditors. Late/out-of-temperature results: troubleshooting-only. Review calibration/blanks/duplicates/standards before release; failed checks require flagging/investigation/documented correction-or-rejection. Verify turbidity/particle mixing/settling/range and residual reagent/contact/measurement timing. Field readings provisional pending same-location/time-window laboratory comparison; notify Chief Operator when confirmation contradicts adjustment. Storm sampling increases until raw/settled stability. SCADA Historian Server (Lantern) retains doses/analyzers/filter-status/washes/comments/shared timestamps;

New part:
S101: Planned maintenance is controlled through a work order process that ties each task to an approved operating window, a named responsible person, and a defined return-to-service condition.
S102: The Chief Operator reviews the next-day schedule with operations staff so that treatment capacity, water quality risk, and distribution demand are understood before work is released.
S103: The Maintenance Planner is also known as Quarry for internal radio coordination during maintenance planning discussions.
S104: The Maintenance Planner verifies that each work order identifies affected equipment, required isolations, parts staging, and the evidence needed to close the work.
S105: The Maintenance Planner uses the snapshot to compare planned rake work against recent mechanical loading before releasing the task package.
S106: The Duty Engineer checks proposed work against current operating constraints and may defer nonessential activity when treatment margin is limited.
S107: Lockout planning identifies electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, chemical, and stored-energy hazards before personnel enter or service plant equipment.
S108: Field isolation is verified locally by the assigned craft worker and then acknowledged by operations before the equipment is opened, adjusted, or tested.
S109: Ironwood shall remain unavailable for routine maintenance release until isolation points are tagged, verified locally, and acknowledged in the shift turnover record.
S110: Work in the North Filter Gallery and South Filter Gallery is scheduled to keep enough filtration capacity available for expected demand and wash cycles.
S111: Any planned change affecting the Clearwell Level Controller requires coordination with the High Service Pump Header operating plan before the change is applied.
S112: The Chemical Supplier Driver sends the Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log before unloading any replacement cylinders at the plant.
S113: Supplier access is limited to approved routes, assigned unloading areas, and times when an operator is available to observe chemical connections and vehicle movement.
S114: Deliveries for the Coagulant Dosing Skid are staged so that hoses, containment, and emergency washdown equipment are inspected before transfer begins.
S115: Chemical work near the Chlorine Contact Basin is coordinated with operating staff so that ventilation, gas monitoring, and communications are available during the task.
S116: Shift communication includes the status of open isolations, temporary operating limits, unavailable equipment, and any abnormal condition that could affect the next crew.
S117: The Distribution Dispatcher is informed before maintenance changes the availability of the High Service Pump Header, North Distribution Pressure Station, or South Distribution Pressure Station.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
